answer.why_different: The generated side adds a callback Path Item at the runtime-expression location, including a POST operation, request body, and responses, whereas the official side has no such callback. This is primarily a different structure. The generated callback is also reported as not valid OpenAPI 3.0 because the callback value is missing the required '$ref' property. In addition, for notifyMOIChanges, the specification requires an mOIChanges array, which is not present in the generated callback payload.
answer.spec_3gpp: The 3GPP specification defines Notification Target as a POST resource and maps notifyMOIChanges to POST at {notificationTarget}. Its required notification fields include href, notificationId, notificationType, eventTime, systemDN, and mOIChanges. The generated payload includes the first five but omits mOIChanges.
answer.openapi: OpenAPI 3.0 permits a callback map whose expression key identifies a callback URL and whose value is a Path Item Object; the callback may contain a POST operation. However, the supplied validation result states that this generated callback is not valid OpenAPI 3.0 because '$ref' is required, so it breaks the OpenAPI format under the stated rule.
answer.clearer_why: The official side is absent and therefore does not explain the notification callback. The generated side makes the intended POST callback, payload, and success/error responses visible, although it must be corrected to be valid OpenAPI and to represent the required mOIChanges field.

##### Runtime Expressions  
Runtime expressions allow defining values based on information that will only be available within the HTTP message in an actual API call.
This mechanism is used by [Link Objects](#link-object) and [Callback Objects](#callback-object).  
The runtime expression is defined by the following [ABNF](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5234) syntax  
```
expression = ( "$url" | "$method" | "$statusCode" | "$request." source | "$response." source )
